key_insight: Fe or Cr substitution strengthens the six studied Ni grain boundaries, with cohesion gains depending on element type and local atomic structure.
engineering_relevance: Atomistically predicted cohesion parameters could inform continuum fracture models for multicomponent Ni-based alloys.
method: Compute DFT rigid-body separation curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni grain boundaries.
Extract work of separation and maximum traction using the universal binding energy relation.
Benchmark ML interatomic potentials against DFT, then sample finer alloy concentrations and ternary configurations.
evidence_signal: One tested ML potential quantitatively matched DFT cohesion metrics and enabled expanded sampling, including Ni56Fe20Cr24 ternary configurations.
watch_item: Binary alloying trends do not quantitatively resolve Fe–Cr interplay; explicit ternary calculations remain necessary.
paper_title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
